::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Is there a better name for a 'three-dimensional coordinate system'?](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/2492181/is-there-a-better-name-for-a-three-dimensional-coordinate-system), asked by [magnolia1](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/406547/magnolia1) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2017-10-27; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> I am wondering if there is a commonly agreed name for any system that makes use of three coordinates. Something that includes 'geographical coordinate system', 'spherical coordinate system', 'celestial coordinat system' and all the likes.
> Or is 'three-dimensional coordinate system' the answer?
> thanks!
:::

Well, $\mathbb{R}^3$ is sometimes called *space*, so I suppose you could use *spatial coordinate system.*  But other than that, I can't think of a name for a coordinate system with three dimensions besides “three-dimensional coordinate system.”
